this table is not.

| Diagnosed visual problem | Candidate technique | Authority / stop |
|---|---|---|
| Meaningful direction, continuous value, or center focus is missing | Linear/radial gradient or channel alpha | §6.2 / §6.3; otherwise keep solid paint |
| Picture/card/overlay elevation or boundary is unclear | Object or picture/carrier shadow, restrained glow, or hairline | §6.4; one light direction |
| Native copy and image do not integrate | Scrim, fade, wash, vignette, off-center spotlight, or faux glass | §6.5 and the Image-Treatment Implementation Map; verify contrast; no backdrop blur |
| Relationship state, direction, continuity, or boundary is unclear | Draft/optional/future → dash; direction → marker; undirected → solid; continuous flow → gradient stroke; repeated boundary → frame/contour/crop edge; exact grid → multi-subpath | §6.6 / §6.3; every line needs a job |
| Body copy carries a load-bearing figure, contrast, or noun that does not survive a scan | Inline emphasis run — a nested `<tspan>` with its own fill or weight inside the same paragraph | §6.7; the frame stays one editable text object |
| Short display text needs notation, silhouette, or material/image emphasis | Removed/former → strike; eyebrow distinction → tracking; display silhouette → outline/gradient; justified material/image emphasis → native picture/texture fill; luminous metric → glow; semantic list → native bullet | §6.7 / §6.3 / §6.4; no decorative body-copy treatment |
| Tilt, repetition, or reversible asset direction helps composition | Rotate, translate/mirror, or local `<use>` | §6.8; never mirror text, logos, or directional evidence |
| Resolved style needs hand, print, pixel, facets, layers, ribbon, or line-plus-area | Matching constructed recipe | §6.11; no generic decorative freeform |
| Meaning needs an unmatched silhouette, radial hierarchy, gauge, or custom route | Freeform, explicit arc/sector, or calculated arrowhead | §6.9 / §6.10; prefer an equal stock shape/marker |
| Look depends on dense texture, source blur, per-pixel composite, reflection, or skew | Native-safe alternative or prepared/baked asset | §6.12; text/data stay editable |

#### Image-Treatment Implementation Map

**Reference — not a constraint**: when image composition names one of these
modifier or prepared-asset treatments, resolve its implementation here.
`Effect-only` keeps a visible capability here without restoring a layout ID.

| Image handles / treatment | Construction / boundary |
|---|---|
| `M2 · 01/03/04/08/09` · scrim, wash, fade, grid | Explicit solid/linear/radial layers over one picture; §6.2 / §6.3 / §6.5 |
| `M2 · 06/07` · atmospheric wash, watermark/receded field | Reduced picture alpha + optional wash; subordinate to native content; §6.2 / §6.5 |
| `M2 · 02/05` · vignette or spotlight | Radial layer with movable `fx/fy` or `cx/cy`; outer geometry `Approximate`; §6.3 / §6.5 |
| `M3 · 04` · lifted picture panel / visible overlay edge | Picture/carrier shadow, glow, or hairline; shadow one support shape for a framed/captioned panel; §6.4 |
| `M3 · 01/02/05` · frame, print frame, contour/cut edge | Registered native stroke/path; §6.6 |
| `M3 · 03; M1 · 09` · rotation, misregistration, Riso offset | Transform + explicit duplicate layers; §6.8 / §6.11 |
| `M1 · 03` + effect-only forms · paper cut, facets/folds, ribbon, staging | Ordered paths/facets + consistent paint/light; §6.11 / [`native-shape-authoring.md`](./native-shape-authoring.md) §7 |
| `M1 · 01/02/04–08` · crop, opening, subtraction, reveal | Direct clip or materialized Boolean; no `<mask>`; §1.2 / [`native-shape-authoring.md`](./native-shape-authoring.md) §6 |
| Effect-only · faux glass | Visible field + translucent panel + highlight; no blur or frosted-crop substitution; §6.5 |
| `A1 · 02–04; A3 · 02/03` · blur, duotone, blend, frost, desaturation | Prepared local bitmap/composite/derivative; registered frost is a blurred derivative; §6.12 |

**Reference — illustrative colors**: colors below demonstrate syntax only;
generated pages choose paint from the Default locked or Quick-resolved identity
anchors, visual style, content semantics, and current composition. A contextual
tint, gradient stop, shadow/glow paint, or one-off display color need not
already be a persistent identity role; promote it only when it becomes a
recurring named role. Review an `Approximate` result in native PPTX when the
effect carries material meaning.

---

### 6.2 Color, Alpha, and Opacity

Write solid paint as uppercase `#RRGGBB`, `none`, or an exact local `url(#id)`.
Put alpha on the channel that owns it — `fill-opacity`, `stroke-opacity`,
`stop-opacity`, or `flood-opacity` as a unitless `0..1` — and use element
`opacity` only for an `<image>` or one non-group atomic object that fades all
of its channels together. Do not use element `opacity` as an alias for
`rgba()` on a fill-only object, and prefer descendant alpha over group opacity
(§2.2). Alpha multiplies down the tree: color alpha × ancestor group opacity ×
element opacity × channel opacity. Named colors, short/alpha HEX, `rgb()` /
`hsl()`, and percentages remain compatible input that the checker only
recommends normalizing.

---

### 6.3 Gradients and Paint Effects

A gradient is a direct `<linearGradient>` / `<radialGradient>` in `<defs>` with
≥2 explicit-color stops at non-decreasing `0..1` offsets, referenced by exact
`url(#id)`, in `objectBoundingBox` units — no `gradientTransform`,
`spreadMethod`, or CSS gradients. Linear exports as an angle
(`Native-normalized`); radial keeps only its focus point and normalizes the
outer circle to the object (`Approximate`), so place the hotspot with `fx/fy`
inside the object and expect the rim to differ. Text takes gradient fill only;
images take no gradient paint (use §6.5 overlays). A gradient *stroke* needs a
path with both width and height — a perfectly horizontal or vertical gradient
ribbon disappears, so author it as a closed gradient-filled band. Stop colors
are contextual paint: keep them coherent with the deck anchors and page
intent without duplicating a lock row.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="flow" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#2563EB"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#10B981" stop-opacity="0.7"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<path d="M100 200 C260 80 420 320 620 180" fill="none"
      stroke="url(#flow)" stroke-width="12"/>
```

**Native text picture/texture fill**: when the design calls for a photograph,
material, or texture inside editable glyphs, fill the `<text>` (or a
non-positional `<tspan>`) with a registered single-image `<pattern>` marked
`data-pptx-text-image-fill="stretch"` or `"tile"`. It exports as a PowerPoint
run picture fill (`stretch` `Native-normalized`; `tile` needs visual review),
not as a general SVG pattern; the text stays editable. The glyphs are the
only thing showing the image, so the fill must read as one value against the
ground — a near-uniform texture or material, not a scene, gradient, or
anything with its own light and dark regions, which breaks the letterforms
into unreadable patches (a 2026-09-10 cover title was lost this way).

           patternUnits="objectBoundingBox"
           patternContentUnits="objectBoundingBox" width="1" height="1">
    <image href="../images/cloud-texture.png"
           x="0" y="0" width="1" height="1"
           preserveAspectRatio="none"/>
  </pattern>
</defs>
<text x="96" y="220" fill="url(#titleTexture)" fill-opacity="0.85"
      font-family="Microsoft YaHei" font-size="72" font-weight="700">
  国风之美
</text>
```

Preset patterns are a separate PPT interface in [`native-data-interface.md`](./native-data-interface.md).

### 6.4 Shadows, Glow, and Elevation

A filter is native-effect metadata, not a pixel-filter surface: one direct
`<defs><filter>` referenced as a direct `filter="url(#id)"` on a `<rect>`,
`<circle>`, `<polygon>`, `<image>`, `<path>`, `<text>`, or a helper-authored preset group,
built from `feDropShadow` or the blur + flood + composite + merge graph below
with explicit `stdDeviation`, `dx`/`dy`, and `flood-opacity`. A meaningful
offset becomes one outer shadow; zero offset — even `feDropShadow` with
`dx="0" dy="0"` — becomes one glow. Both are `Approximate`: one filter, one
DrawingML effect. Filters on `<tspan>` or ordinary `<g>` and every other
primitive are forbidden; use an existing accent color for glow, since black
reads as diffuse shadow.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-20%" width="130%" height="150%">
    <feDropShadow dx="0" dy="6" stdDeviation="8"
                  flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.10"/>
  </filter>
  <filter id="expandedShadow" x="-15%" y="-20%" width="130%" height="150%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8" result="b"/>
    <feOffset in="b" dx="0" dy="6" result="o"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.10" result="c"/>
    <feComposite in="c" in2="o" operator="in" result="s"/>
    <feMerge><feMergeNode in="s"/><feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/></feMerge>
  </filter>
  <filter id="titleGlow" x="-30%" y="-30%" width="160%" height="160%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="6" result="b"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#38BDF8" flood-opacity="0.45" result="c"/>
    <feComposite in="c" in2="b" operator="in" result="g"/>
    <feMerge><feMergeNode in="g"/><feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/></feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
```

| Elevation | Use | `dy` | `stdDeviation` | Alpha |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Floor | Backgrounds, dividers, equal peers, body containers, decorative lines/icons, single-layer pages | — | — | — |
| Resting | Card over photo/panel, secondary callout | 2–4 | 4–8 | 0.06–0.10 |
| Raised | Primary CTA, focused card, overlay | 6–10 | 10–16 | 0.12–0.20 |
| Glow | Short display text, metric, focus accent | 0 offset | 4–8 | 0.35–0.55 |

**Default — one light source per page (may override when every affected layer
uses one deliberate alternative direction)**: every `feOffset` shadow on one
slide shares the same `dx`/`dy` direction (default `dx="0"`,
`dy="4"`–`dy="8"`, light from upper front). Contradictory shadow directions
make one plane read as several incompatible surfaces. A deliberate upward
paper-layer treatment flips every affected layer together, so one plane keeps
one light direction.

**Reference — not a constraint**: use no more elevation categories than the
hierarchy needs; a page may reuse one category across several related objects,
but two or three shadowed objects usually read cleanest — check that a fourth
earns its weight. Pick one weight tool per container — shadow, border,
gradient fill, or strong tint — never stacked; peer-grid cards, dividers,
body containers, and background panels stay on the floor.
Same-family colored shadow is reserved for a focal accent. On dark backgrounds
a light hairline or restrained glow separates surfaces; glow on body copy
reduces legibility. For older/strict renderers, replace a filter with two or
three offset translucent shapes behind the object: alpha `0.03–0.05`,
increasing offset/radius, and optional same-family tint near `0.04`
(`Native-stable`).

### 6.5 Image Treatments, Overlays, and Glass-like Surfaces

| Need | Authoring contract | Fidelity |
|---|---|---|
| Cover/crop | Readable raster dimensions + aligned `slice` | Native `srcRect`; `Native-stable` |
| Contain/fit | Aligned `meet` | Fitted picture frame; `Native-normalized` |
| Stretch | `preserveAspectRatio="none"` | Native stretched frame |
| Uniform fade | `<image opacity="...">` | Native picture alpha |
| Shaped picture | §1.2 image-only `clip-path` | Preset/custom picture geometry |

Every `<image>` has explicit positive `width`/`height`, one decodable
project-local or data-URI `href`, and — when not the default `xMidYMid meet` —
an aligned `preserveAspectRatio` with explicit `meet` or `slice`, or `none`
alone. A clip disables `meet` frame-fit, so match the box to the source ratio
or use `slice`; put a §6.4 filter directly on an unclipped image, and for a
clipped one on an exact outer `<g>` whose sole visual child is that image —
never both on the same `<image>`. A nested `<svg>` is only the exact
single-image crop wrapper the crop parser accepts, not a general viewport;
its required form (outer `preserveAspectRatio="none"` + `overflow="hidden"`
+ unit-space `viewBox`, child `<image>` at `0 0 1 1`) is in
[`svg-contract.md`](../scripts/docs/svg-contract.md) under "Nested SVG is
picture-crop transport".

| Overlay | Construction | Typical stops / alpha |
|---|---|---|
| Directional scrim | Linear rect, darkest beside text | `0%: 0.88; 55%: 0.30; 100%: 0` |
| Bottom title fade | Vertical rect over lower image | black `0 → 0.72` |
| Vignette/spotlight | Radial rect; place the hotspot with `fx/fy` or `cx/cy` inside the canonical focus circle; outer center/radius remain approximate | black `0 → 0.58` |
| Brand wash | Directional existing brand-color gradient | `0.80 → 0.10` |
| Grid scrim | Seamless no-stroke rect cells over one image; vary neighboring alpha narrowly and irregularly | Keep the field subordinate; a regular alternation reads as a checkerboard |
| Faux glass | Visible fields + diagonal linear panel (`0,0 → 1,1`) + highlight stroke; optional §6.4 elevation | white `0.38 → 0.12`; stroke about `0.55` |

Layer in document order: image → scrim/wash → text. True source/backdrop blur is
`Bake-required`; faux glass is explicit layering, not blur. Validate contrast
against the actual image. All overlay gradients follow §6.3 linear/radial
fidelity.

### 6.6 Lines, Connectors, Borders, and Markers

A solid stroke with width and alpha is an editable native line. Dashes map to
the five presets (`4,4` / `6,3` dash, `2,2` sysDot, `8,4` lgDash, `8,4,2,4`
lgDashDot) or to one custom `dash gap` pair; caps are `butt` / `round` /
`square`, joins `miter` / `round` / `bevel`, `vector-effect` `none` or
`non-scaling-stroke`. Markers follow §1.1 (type native, size approximate); a
gradient stroke follows §6.3.

**Default — relationship-fit dash rhythm (may override when style calls for
another rhythm)**: after §6.1 selects dash, preserve direction markers and
branch-owned placeholder patterns.

| Already-dashed/dotted job (illustrative) | Dash |
|---|---|
| Separator/boundary | `4,4` |
| Subtle dotted border/generic non-image placeholder | `2,2` |
| Optional/future timeline/flow connector | `8,4` |
| Technical/dimension line | `8,4,2,4` |

**Default — contour-fit joins (may override when the resolved style calls for
another character)**: smooth polyline/organic form → `round`; technical
diagram → `bevel`; crisp rectangle/arrow → `miter`.

```xml
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12"
  fill="none" stroke="#999999" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
<line x1="100" y1="420" x2="500" y2="420"
  stroke="#1A73E8" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="8,4"/>
<polyline points="100,200 200,100 300,200" fill="none"
  stroke="#1A73E8" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
```

Match marker paint to the parent stroke using the shape-specific channel from
§1.1: fill for closed/oval line ends and stroke for the open arrow. Use markers
for connectors and §6.10 calculated geometry for a manual diagonal arrowhead.
When exact grid spacing matters, use one multi-subpath path rather than a
fixed-density preset pattern:

```xml
<path d="M40 0V120 M80 0V120 M0 40H120 M0 80H120"
      fill="none" stroke="#2E6EA8" stroke-width="0.8"/>
```

### 6.7 Advanced Text Treatments

Generated text uses only the canonical values: `font-weight` `normal` / `bold`
/ an integer hundred, `font-style` `normal` / `italic`, `text-anchor` on
`<text>` or above, `text-decoration` `underline` / `line-through` / both,
direct `baseline-shift="super|sub"` on `<tspan>`, and unitless-px
`letter-spacing` and `font-size`. Inheritable text declarations belong only on
`<svg>`, `<g>`, `<text>`, or `<tspan>`; `xml:space` (`default` or `preserve`) on
`<text>` / `<tspan>` is the one whitespace control — it inherits through the
text tree and may be reset on a child `<tspan>`, so one frame can mix
collapsed and preserved runs. Every other `font-*` / `text-*`
property has no native mapping and is an error.

| Treatment | SVG surface | Result / boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Underline / strike / both | `text-decoration="underline"`, `line-through`, or both | `Native-stable`; both emits both run properties |
| Mixed runs | Non-positional `<tspan>` | One `Native-normalized` editable frame; §4.2 |
| Superscript / subscript | Direct `baseline-shift="super|sub"` on `<tspan>` | Editable run at PowerPoint's native baseline offset; set `font-size` on the same run when a smaller glyph is intended |
| Tracking | Unitless-px `letter-spacing` | `Native-normalized`; negative tracking must leave every run a positive advance |
| Transparency | `opacity` / `fill-opacity` on text/run | `Native-normalized` run alpha, not isolated compositing |
| Gradient fill | §6.3 gradient on text/run | Editable fill; geometry normalizes |
| Outline | Solid `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-opacity` | `Native-normalized` editable run outline; re-import does not reconstruct it |
| Shadow/glow | §6.4 filter on `<text>` only | Shape shadow / run glow; `Approximate` |
| Native bullet | Leading `· • ● ▪ ■ ◆ ◇ ◦ ‣` + non-empty content | `·`/`•` → `•`; others unchanged; color/alpha from marker run; font/size follow text |

**Inline emphasis**: bold or accent-colored `<tspan>` runs lift numerical
results, explicit contrasts, or a load-bearing noun inside prose; green/red
conventionally read as polarity.

<text x="80" y="200" font-size="20" fill="#333333">

</text>

### 6.2 Color, Alpha, and Opacity

Write solid paint as uppercase `#RRGGBB`, `none`, or an exact local `url(#id)`.
Put alpha on the channel that owns it — `fill-opacity`, `stroke-opacity`,
`stop-opacity`, or `flood-opacity` as a unitless `0..1` — and use element
`opacity` only for an `<image>` or one non-group atomic object that fades all
of its channels together. Do not use element `opacity` as an alias for
`rgba()` on a fill-only object, and prefer descendant alpha over group opacity
(§2.2). Alpha multiplies down the tree: color alpha × ancestor group opacity ×
element opacity × channel opacity. Named colors, short/alpha HEX, `rgb()` /
`hsl()`, and percentages remain compatible input that the checker only
recommends normalizing.

### 6.3 Gradients and Paint Effects

A gradient is a direct `<linearGradient>` / `<radialGradient>` in `<defs>` with
≥2 explicit-color stops at non-decreasing `0..1` offsets, referenced by exact
`url(#id)`, in `objectBoundingBox` units — no `gradientTransform`,
`spreadMethod`, or CSS gradients. Linear exports as an angle
(`Native-normalized`); radial keeps only its focus point and normalizes the
outer circle to the object (`Approximate`), so place the hotspot with `fx/fy`
inside the object and expect the rim to differ. Text takes gradient fill only;
images take no gradient paint (use §6.5 overlays). A gradient *stroke* needs a
path with both width and height — a perfectly horizontal or vertical gradient
ribbon disappears, so author it as a closed gradient-filled band. Stop colors
are contextual paint: keep them coherent with the deck anchors and page
intent without duplicating a lock row.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="flow" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#2563EB"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#10B981" stop-opacity="0.7"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<path d="M100 200 C260 80 420 320 620 180" fill="none"
      stroke="url(#flow)" stroke-width="12"/>

### 6.7 Advanced Text Treatments

Generated text uses only the canonical values: `font-weight` `normal` / `bold`
/ an integer hundred, `font-style` `normal` / `italic`, `text-anchor` on

direct `baseline-shift="super|sub"` on `<tspan>`, and unitless-px

`<svg>`, `<g>`, `<text>`, or `<tspan>`; `xml:space` (`default` or `preserve`) on

text tree and may be reset on a child `<tspan>`, so one frame can mix
collapsed and preserved runs. Every other `font-*` / `text-*`
property has no native mapping and is an error.

| Treatment | SVG surface | Result / boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Underline / strike / both | `text-decoration="underline"`, `line-through`, or both | `Native-stable`; both emits both run properties |
| Mixed runs | Non-positional `<tspan>` | One `Native-normalized` editable frame; §4.2 |
| Superscript / subscript | Direct `baseline-shift="super|sub"` on `<tspan>` | Editable run at PowerPoint's native baseline offset; set `font-size` on the same run when a smaller glyph is intended |
| Tracking | Unitless-px `letter-spacing` | `Native-normalized`; negative tracking must leave every run a positive advance |
| Transparency | `opacity` / `fill-opacity` on text/run | `Native-normalized` run alpha, not isolated compositing |
| Gradient fill | §6.3 gradient on text/run | Editable fill; geometry normalizes |
| Outline | Solid `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-opacity` | `Native-normalized` editable run outline; re-import does not reconstruct it |
| Shadow/glow | §6.4 filter on `<text>` only | Shape shadow / run glow; `Approximate` |
| Native bullet | Leading `· • ● ▪ ■ ◆ ◇ ◦ ‣` + non-empty content | `·`/`•` → `•`; others unchanged; color/alpha from marker run; font/size follow text |

results, explicit contrasts, or a load-bearing noun inside prose; green/red
conventionally read as polarity.

### 6.2 Color, Alpha, and Opacity

Write solid paint as uppercase `#RRGGBB`, `none`, or an exact local `url(#id)`.
Put alpha on the channel that owns it — `fill-opacity`, `stroke-opacity`,
`stop-opacity`, or `flood-opacity` as a unitless `0..1` — and use element
`opacity` only for an `<image>` or one non-group atomic object that fades all
of its channels together. Do not use element `opacity` as an alias for
`rgba()` on a fill-only object, and prefer descendant alpha over group opacity
(§2.2). Alpha multiplies down the tree: color alpha × ancestor group opacity ×
element opacity × channel opacity. Named colors, short/alpha HEX, `rgb()` /
`hsl()`, and percentages remain compatible input that the checker only
recommends normalizing.

---

### 6.3 Gradients and Paint Effects

A gradient is a direct `<linearGradient>` / `<radialGradient>` in `<defs>` with
≥2 explicit-color stops at non-decreasing `0..1` offsets, referenced by exact
`url(#id)`, in `objectBoundingBox` units — no `gradientTransform`,
`spreadMethod`, or CSS gradients. Linear exports as an angle
(`Native-normalized`); radial keeps only its focus point and normalizes the
outer circle to the object (`Approximate`), so place the hotspot with `fx/fy`
inside the object and expect the rim to differ. Text takes gradient fill only;
images take no gradient paint (use §6.5 overlays). A gradient *stroke* needs a
path with both width and height — a perfectly horizontal or vertical gradient
ribbon disappears, so author it as a closed gradient-filled band. Stop colors
are contextual paint: keep them coherent with the deck anchors and page
intent without duplicating a lock row.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="flow" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#2563EB"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#10B981" stop-opacity="0.7"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<path d="M100 200 C260 80 420 320 620 180" fill="none"
      stroke="url(#flow)" stroke-width="12"/>
```

**Native text picture/texture fill**: when the design calls for a photograph,
material, or texture inside editable glyphs, fill the `<text>` (or a
non-positional `<tspan>`) with a registered single-image `<pattern>` marked
`data-pptx-text-image-fill="stretch"` or `"tile"`. It exports as a PowerPoint
run picture fill (`stretch` `Native-normalized`; `tile` needs visual review),
not as a general SVG pattern; the text stays editable. The glyphs are the
only thing showing the image, so the fill must read as one value against the
ground — a near-uniform texture or material, not a scene, gradient, or
anything with its own light and dark regions, which breaks the letterforms
into unreadable patches (a 2026-09-10 cover title was lost this way).

```xml
<defs>
  <pattern id="titleTexture" data-pptx-text-image-fill="stretch"
           patternUnits="objectBoundingBox"
           patternContentUnits="objectBoundingBox" width="1" height="1">
    <image href="../images/cloud-texture.png"
           x="0" y="0" width="1" height="1"
           preserveAspectRatio="none"/>
  </pattern>
</defs>
<text x="96" y="220" fill="url(#titleTexture)" fill-opacity="0.85"
      font-family="Microsoft YaHei" font-size="72" font-weight="700">
  国风之美
</text>
```

Preset patterns are a separate PPT interface in [`native-data-interface.md`](./native-data-interface.md).

### 6.4 Shadows, Glow, and Elevation

A filter is native-effect metadata, not a pixel-filter surface: one direct
`<defs><filter>` referenced as a direct `filter="url(#id)"` on a `<rect>`,
`<circle>`, `<polygon>`, `<image>`, `<path>`, `<text>`, or a helper-authored preset group,
built from `feDropShadow` or the blur + flood + composite + merge graph below
with explicit `stdDeviation`, `dx`/`dy`, and `flood-opacity`. A meaningful
offset becomes one outer shadow; zero offset — even `feDropShadow` with
`dx="0" dy="0"` — becomes one glow. Both are `Approximate`: one filter, one
DrawingML effect. Filters on `<tspan>` or ordinary `<g>` and every other
primitive are forbidden; use an existing accent color for glow, since black
reads as diffuse shadow.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-20%" width="130%" height="150%">
    <feDropShadow dx="0" dy="6" stdDeviation="8"
                  flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.10"/>
  </filter>
  <filter id="expandedShadow" x="-15%" y="-20%" width="130%" height="150%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8" result="b"/>
    <feOffset in="b" dx="0" dy="6" result="o"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.10" result="c"/>
    <feComposite in="c" in2="o" operator="in" result="s"/>
    <feMerge><feMergeNode in="s"/><feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/></feMerge>
  </filter>
  <filter id="titleGlow" x="-30%" y="-30%" width="160%" height="160%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="6" result="b"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#38BDF8" flood-opacity="0.45" result="c"/>
    <feComposite in="c" in2="b" operator="in" result="g"/>
    <feMerge><feMergeNode in="g"/><feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/></feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
```

| Elevation | Use | `dy` | `stdDeviation` | Alpha |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Floor | Backgrounds, dividers, equal peers, body containers, decorative lines/icons, single-layer pages | — | — | — |
| Resting | Card over photo/panel, secondary callout | 2–4 | 4–8 | 0.06–0.10 |
| Raised | Primary CTA, focused card, overlay | 6–10 | 10–16 | 0.12–0.20 |
| Glow | Short display text, metric, focus accent | 0 offset | 4–8 | 0.35–0.55 |

**Default — one light source per page (may override when every affected layer
uses one deliberate alternative direction)**: every `feOffset` shadow on one
slide shares the same `dx`/`dy` direction (default `dx="0"`,
`dy="4"`–`dy="8"`, light from upper front). Contradictory shadow directions
make one plane read as several incompatible surfaces. A deliberate upward
paper-layer treatment flips every affected layer together, so one plane keeps
one light direction.

**Reference — not a constraint**: use no more elevation categories than the
hierarchy needs; a page may reuse one category across several related objects,
but two or three shadowed objects usually read cleanest — check that a fourth
earns its weight. Pick one weight tool per container — shadow, border,
gradient fill, or strong tint — never stacked; peer-grid cards, dividers,
body containers, and background panels stay on the floor.
Same-family colored shadow is reserved for a focal accent. On dark backgrounds
a light hairline or restrained glow separates surfaces; glow on body copy
reduces legibility. For older/strict renderers, replace a filter with two or
three offset translucent shapes behind the object: alpha `0.03–0.05`,
increasing offset/radius, and optional same-family tint near `0.04`
(`Native-stable`).

### 6.5 Image Treatments, Overlays, and Glass-like Surfaces

| Need | Authoring contract | Fidelity |
|---|---|---|
| Cover/crop | Readable raster dimensions + aligned `slice` | Native `srcRect`; `Native-stable` |
| Contain/fit | Aligned `meet` | Fitted picture frame; `Native-normalized` |
| Stretch | `preserveAspectRatio="none"` | Native stretched frame |
| Uniform fade | `<image opacity="...">` | Native picture alpha |
| Shaped picture | §1.2 image-only `clip-path` | Preset/custom picture geometry |

Every `<image>` has explicit positive `width`/`height`, one decodable
project-local or data-URI `href`, and — when not the default `xMidYMid meet` —
an aligned `preserveAspectRatio` with explicit `meet` or `slice`, or `none`
alone. A clip disables `meet` frame-fit, so match the box to the source ratio
or use `slice`; put a §6.4 filter directly on an unclipped image, and for a
clipped one on an exact outer `<g>` whose sole visual child is that image —
never both on the same `<image>`. A nested `<svg>` is only the exact
single-image crop wrapper the crop parser accepts, not a general viewport;
its required form (outer `preserveAspectRatio="none"` + `overflow="hidden"`
+ unit-space `viewBox`, child `<image>` at `0 0 1 1`) is in
[`svg-contract.md`](../scripts/docs/svg-contract.md) under "Nested SVG is
picture-crop transport".

| Overlay | Construction | Typical stops / alpha |
|---|---|---|
| Directional scrim | Linear rect, darkest beside text | `0%: 0.88; 55%: 0.30; 100%: 0` |
| Bottom title fade | Vertical rect over lower image | black `0 → 0.72` |
| Vignette/spotlight | Radial rect; place the hotspot with `fx/fy` or `cx/cy` inside the canonical focus circle; outer center/radius remain approximate | black `0 → 0.58` |
| Brand wash | Directional existing brand-color gradient | `0.80 → 0.10` |
| Grid scrim | Seamless no-stroke rect cells over one image; vary neighboring alpha narrowly and irregularly | Keep the field subordinate; a regular alternation reads as a checkerboard |
| Faux glass | Visible fields + diagonal linear panel (`0,0 → 1,1`) + highlight stroke; optional §6.4 elevation | white `0.38 → 0.12`; stroke about `0.55` |

Layer in document order: image → scrim/wash → text. True source/backdrop blur is
`Bake-required`; faux glass is explicit layering, not blur. Validate contrast
against the actual image. All overlay gradients follow §6.3 linear/radial
fidelity.

(§2.2). Alpha multiplies down the tree: color alpha × ancestor group opacity ×
element opacity × channel opacity. Named colors, short/alpha HEX, `rgb()` /
`hsl()`, and percentages remain compatible input that the checker only
recommends normalizing.

### 6.3 Gradients and Paint Effects

A gradient is a direct `<linearGradient>` / `<radialGradient>` in `<defs>` with
≥2 explicit-color stops at non-decreasing `0..1` offsets, referenced by exact
`url(#id)`, in `objectBoundingBox` units — no `gradientTransform`,
`spreadMethod`, or CSS gradients. Linear exports as an angle
(`Native-normalized`); radial keeps only its focus point and normalizes the
outer circle to the object (`Approximate`), so place the hotspot with `fx/fy`
inside the object and expect the rim to differ. Text takes gradient fill only;
images take no gradient paint (use §6.5 overlays). A gradient *stroke* needs a
path with both width and height — a perfectly horizontal or vertical gradient
ribbon disappears, so author it as a closed gradient-filled band. Stop colors
are contextual paint: keep them coherent with the deck anchors and page
intent without duplicating a lock row.

```xml
<defs>
  <linearGradient id="flow" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
    <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#2563EB"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#10B981" stop-opacity="0.7"/>
  </linearGradient>
</defs>
<path d="M100 200 C260 80 420 320 620 180" fill="none"
      stroke="url(#flow)" stroke-width="12"/>
```

**Native text picture/texture fill**: when the design calls for a photograph,
material, or texture inside editable glyphs, fill the `<text>` (or a
non-positional `<tspan>`) with a registered single-image `<pattern>` marked
`data-pptx-text-image-fill="stretch"` or `"tile"`. It exports as a PowerPoint
run picture fill (`stretch` `Native-normalized`; `tile` needs visual review),
not as a general SVG pattern; the text stays editable. The glyphs are the
only thing showing the image, so the fill must read as one value against the
ground — a near-uniform texture or material, not a scene, gradient, or
anything with its own light and dark regions, which breaks the letterforms
into unreadable patches (a 2026-09-10 cover title was lost this way).

```xml
<defs>
  <pattern id="titleTexture" data-pptx-text-image-fill="stretch"
           patternUnits="objectBoundingBox"
           patternContentUnits="objectBoundingBox" width="1" height="1">
    <image href="../images/cloud-texture.png"
           x="0" y="0" width="1" height="1"
           preserveAspectRatio="none"/>
  </pattern>
</defs>
<text x="96" y="220" fill="url(#titleTexture)" fill-opacity="0.85"
      font-family="Microsoft YaHei" font-size="72" font-weight="700">
  国风之美
</text>
```

Preset patterns are a separate PPT interface in [`native-data-interface.md`](./native-data-interface.md).

### 6.4 Shadows, Glow, and Elevation

A filter is native-effect metadata, not a pixel-filter surface: one direct
`<defs><filter>` referenced as a direct `filter="url(#id)"` on a `<rect>`,
`<circle>`, `<polygon>`, `<image>`, `<path>`, `<text>`, or a helper-authored preset group,
built from `feDropShadow` or the blur + flood + composite + merge graph below
with explicit `stdDeviation`, `dx`/`dy`, and `flood-opacity`. A meaningful
offset becomes one outer shadow; zero offset — even `feDropShadow` with
`dx="0" dy="0"` — becomes one glow. Both are `Approximate`: one filter, one
DrawingML effect. Filters on `<tspan>` or ordinary `<g>` and every other
primitive are forbidden; use an existing accent color for glow, since black
reads as diffuse shadow.

```xml
<defs>
  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-20%" width="130%" height="150%">
    <feDropShadow dx="0" dy="6" stdDeviation="8"
                  flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.10"/>
  </filter>
  <filter id="expandedShadow" x="-15%" y="-20%" width="130%" height="150%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8" result="b"/>
    <feOffset in="b" dx="0" dy="6" result="o"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.10" result="c"/>
    <feComposite in="c" in2="o" operator="in" result="s"/>
    <feMerge><feMergeNode in="s"/><feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/></feMerge>
  </filter>
  <filter id="titleGlow" x="-30%" y="-30%" width="160%" height="160%">
    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="6" result="b"/>
    <feFlood flood-color="#38BDF8" flood-opacity="0.45" result="c"/>
    <feComposite in="c" in2="b" operator="in" result="g"/>
    <feMerge><feMergeNode in="g"/><feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/></feMerge>
  </filter>
</defs>
```

| Elevation | Use | `dy` | `stdDeviation` | Alpha |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Floor | Backgrounds, dividers, equal peers, body containers, decorative lines/icons, single-layer pages | — | — | — |
| Resting | Card over photo/panel, secondary callout | 2–4 | 4–8 | 0.06–0.10 |
| Raised | Primary CTA, focused card, overlay | 6–10 | 10–16 | 0.12–0.20 |
| Glow | Short display text, metric, focus accent | 0 offset | 4–8 | 0.35–0.55 |

**Default — one light source per page (may override when every affected layer
uses one deliberate alternative direction)**: every `feOffset` shadow on one
slide shares the same `dx`/`dy` direction (default `dx="0"`,
`dy="4"`–`dy="8"`, light from upper front). Contradictory shadow directions
make one plane read as several incompatible surfaces. A deliberate upward
paper-layer treatment flips every affected layer together, so one plane keeps
one light direction.

**Reference — not a constraint**: use no more elevation categories than the
hierarchy needs; a page may reuse one category across several related objects,
but two or three shadowed objects usually read cleanest — check that a fourth
earns its weight. Pick one weight tool per container — shadow, border,
gradient fill, or strong tint — never stacked; peer-grid cards, dividers,
body containers, and background panels stay on the floor.
Same-family colored shadow is reserved for a focal accent. On dark backgrounds
a light hairline or restrained glow separates surfaces; glow on body copy
reduces legibility. For older/strict renderers, replace a filter with two or
three offset translucent shapes behind the object: alpha `0.03–0.05`,
increasing offset/radius, and optional same-family tint near `0.04`
(`Native-stable`).

### 6.5 Image Treatments, Overlays, and Glass-like Surfaces

| Need | Authoring contract | Fidelity |
|---|---|---|
| Cover/crop | Readable raster dimensions + aligned `slice` | Native `srcRect`; `Native-stable` |
| Contain/fit | Aligned `meet` | Fitted picture frame; `Native-normalized` |
| Stretch | `preserveAspectRatio="none"` | Native stretched frame |
| Uniform fade | `<image opacity="...">` | Native picture alpha |
| Shaped picture | §1.2 image-only `clip-path` | Preset/custom picture geometry |

Every `<image>` has explicit positive `width`/`height`, one decodable
project-local or data-URI `href`, and — when not the default `xMidYMid meet` —
an aligned `preserveAspectRatio` with explicit `meet` or `slice`, or `none`
alone. A clip disables `meet` frame-fit, so match the box to the source ratio
or use `slice`; put a §6.4 filter directly on an unclipped image, and for a
clipped one on an exact outer `<g>` whose sole visual child is that image —
never both on the same `<image>`. A nested `<svg>` is only the exact
single-image crop wrapper the crop parser accepts, not a general viewport;
its required form (outer `preserveAspectRatio="none"` + `overflow="hidden"`
+ unit-space `viewBox`, child `<image>` at `0 0 1 1`) is in
[`svg-contract.md`](../scripts/docs/svg-contract.md) under "Nested SVG is
picture-crop transport".

| Overlay | Construction | Typical stops / alpha |
|---|---|---|
| Directional scrim | Linear rect, darkest beside text | `0%: 0.88; 55%: 0.30; 100%: 0` |
| Bottom title fade | Vertical rect over lower image | black `0 → 0.72` |
| Vignette/spotlight | Radial rect; place the hotspot with `fx/fy` or `cx/cy` inside the canonical focus circle; outer center/radius remain approximate | black `0 → 0.58` |
| Brand wash | Directional existing brand-color gradient | `0.80 → 0.10` |
| Grid scrim | Seamless no-stroke rect cells over one image; vary neighboring alpha narrowly and irregularly | Keep the field subordinate; a regular alternation reads as a checkerboard |
| Faux glass | Visible fields + diagonal linear panel (`0,0 → 1,1`) + highlight stroke; optional §6.4 elevation | white `0.38 → 0.12`; stroke about `0.55` |

Layer in document order: image → scrim/wash → text. True source/backdrop blur is
`Bake-required`; faux glass is explicit layering, not blur. Validate contrast
against the actual image. All overlay gradients follow §6.3 linear/radial
fidelity.

### 6.6 Lines, Connectors, Borders, and Markers

A solid stroke with width and alpha is an editable native line. Dashes map to
the five presets (`4,4` / `6,3` dash, `2,2` sysDot, `8,4` lgDash, `8,4,2,4`
lgDashDot) or to one custom `dash gap` pair; caps are `butt` / `round` /
`square`, joins `miter` / `round` / `bevel`, `vector-effect` `none` or
`non-scaling-stroke`. Markers follow §1.1 (type native, size approximate); a
gradient stroke follows §6.3.

**Default — relationship-fit dash rhythm (may override when style calls for
another rhythm)**: after §6.1 selects dash, preserve direction markers and
branch-owned placeholder patterns.

| Already-dashed/dotted job (illustrative) | Dash |
|---|---|
| Separator/boundary | `4,4` |
| Subtle dotted border/generic non-image placeholder | `2,2` |
| Optional/future timeline/flow connector | `8,4` |
| Technical/dimension line | `8,4,2,4` |

**Default — contour-fit joins (may override when the resolved style calls for
another character)**: smooth polyline/organic form → `round`; technical
diagram → `bevel`; crisp rectangle/arrow → `miter`.

```xml
<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12"
  fill="none" stroke="#999999" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="4,4"/>
<line x1="100" y1="420" x2="500" y2="420"
  stroke="#1A73E8" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="8,4"/>
<polyline points="100,200 200,100 300,200" fill="none"
  stroke="#1A73E8" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
```

Match marker paint to the parent stroke using the shape-specific channel from
§1.1: fill for closed/oval line ends and stroke for the open arrow. Use markers
for connectors and §6.10 calculated geometry for a manual diagonal arrowhead.
When exact grid spacing matters, use one multi-subpath path rather than a
fixed-density preset pattern:

```xml
<path d="M40 0V120 M80 0V120 M0 40H120 M0 80H120"
      fill="none" stroke="#2E6EA8" stroke-width="0.8"/>
```

### 6.7 Advanced Text Treatments

Generated text uses only the canonical values: `font-weight` `normal` / `bold`
/ an integer hundred, `font-style` `normal` / `italic`, `text-anchor` on
`<text>` or above, `text-decoration` `underline` / `line-through` / both,
direct `baseline-shift="super|sub"` on `<tspan>`, and unitless-px
`letter-spacing` and `font-size`. Inheritable text declarations belong only on
`<svg>`, `<g>`, `<text>`, or `<tspan>`; `xml:space` (`default` or `preserve`) on
`<text>` / `<tspan>` is the one whitespace control — it inherits through the
text tree and may be reset on a child `<tspan>`, so one frame can mix
collapsed and preserved runs. Every other `font-*` / `text-*`
property has no native mapping and is an error.

| Treatment | SVG surface | Result / boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Underline / strike / both | `text-decoration="underline"`, `line-through`, or both | `Native-stable`; both emits both run properties |
| Mixed runs | Non-positional `<tspan>` | One `Native-normalized` editable frame; §4.2 |
| Superscript / subscript | Direct `baseline-shift="super|sub"` on `<tspan>` | Editable run at PowerPoint's native baseline offset; set `font-size` on the same run when a smaller glyph is intended |
| Tracking | Unitless-px `letter-spacing` | `Native-normalized`; negative tracking must leave every run a positive advance |
| Transparency | `opacity` / `fill-opacity` on text/run | `Native-normalized` run alpha, not isolated compositing |
| Gradient fill | §6.3 gradient on text/run | Editable fill; geometry normalizes |
| Outline | Solid `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `stroke-opacity` | `Native-normalized` editable run outline; re-import does not reconstruct it |
| Shadow/glow | §6.4 filter on `<text>` only | Shape shadow / run glow; `Approximate` |
| Native bullet | Leading `· • ● ▪ ■ ◆ ◇ ◦ ‣` + non-empty content | `·`/`•` → `•`; others unchanged; color/alpha from marker run; font/size follow text |

**Inline emphasis**: bold or accent-colored `<tspan>` runs lift numerical
results, explicit contrasts, or a load-bearing noun inside prose; green/red
conventionally read as polarity.

For `=no` objects... The native marker is only for `=yes`. But the plot-area comment is for verify-charts calibration. For ChartEx types (waterfall, pareto), §2.2 says "ChartEx (waterfall, funnel, histogram, pareto, treemap, sunburst, box_whisker) takes no axes, plot_area, or data_labels" — that's about the JSON metadata field `plot_area`. The comment marker: the template waterfall has a comment. I'll include the comment (it's the drawing's plot area) but omit `plot_area` from JSON for ChartEx types. Hmm, but §2.1 says the marker is mandatory per verified chart object, and for ChartEx the JSON omits plot_area. OK: comment present, JSON without plot_area.

35:- **Line markers** — `line_style: "lineMarker"` draws a circle at every point in the series colour; `marker_size` (root or per series, SVG px diameter, `2..72` pt after `×0.75`) sizes it. `line_style` itself is a chart-root option — `series[].line_style` is rejected; inside a `combo` it sits on the plot or on a typed series. `series[].point_colors` on a line series marks single points: a colour draws that point's marker in that colour, `null` leaves it bare (with `line_style: "line"` only the coloured points carry markers), so an emphasised endpoint is `[null, …, "#C8102E"]`. Area series draw no markers; a line with markers over a fill is a `combo`. `data_labels` (column, bar, line, and area plots only, combo plots of those types included; pie-family, radar, scatter/bubble, stock, and ChartEx charts reject it — show their values through companion `notes`) is `true` or an object with `show_value`, `position`, `number_format`, `font_size`, `font_family`, `bold`, `color`, per-point `colors`, and `points` (zero-based `idx` plus optional overrides — with an explicit `show_*` flag every point keeps its label and `delete: true` hides one; without one only the listed points are labeled); positions: clustered column/bar `outside_end` / `inside_end` / `inside_base` / `center`, stacked `inside_end` / `inside_base` / `center`, line `above` / `center` / `best_fit`, area none; `series[].data_labels` takes the same object for one series, so two lines can label different points. ---
description: Conditional quality-gate stage for data-chart geometry and encoding verification.
---

# Verify Charts Stage

> Conditional Generate-PPTX quality stage. Run after a deck containing data charts has finished SVG generation and before post-processing/export; it catches coordinate and encoding errors introduced while mapping source values into SVG marks. Default runs it context-independently from `design_spec.md` plus the SVGs; the lockless Quick branch runs in the same active session from the page decisions just authored — if that context is lost, restart Quick rather than inventing a page plan from finished files.

## When to Run

- The deck contains at least one chart where source values determine SVG geometry or encoding (bar lengths, point positions, arc angles, polygon vertices, connector endpoints, bubble centers/radii, flow widths, cell colors, word sizes).
- SVGs exist in `<project_path>/svg_output/` and `finalize_svg.py` / `svg_to_pptx.py` have not run. Default enters from its quality-gate order; Quick runs it before its one lockless final checker.

The calculator has direct models for bars, lines/scatter, pie/donut, radar, and grids. Composite charts are not out of scope: geometry that reduces to repeated direct calculations is `decomposable-calc`; data-driven geometry with no layout model is `manual-verify`, never silently skipped.

---

## Step 1: Build the chart-object list from the active profile authority

| Active profile | Object-list authority |
|---|---|
| Default Generate | `design_spec.md §IX` — every semantic object key whose `Visualization` entry declares value-driven SVG geometry; §VII only resolves a selected catalog reference, and one real §VII data-chart row may supply one legacy object for a page whose §IX predates object keys |
| Quick Generate | The still-active semantic object keys and page decisions, cross-checked one-for-one against every `chart-plot-area` marker found by one search of `svg_output/`; add a missing scoped marker, investigate an unexpected one, keep the list in active context only |

Incidental microvisuals not promoted by the profile authority are not inferred into the list: Default repairs §IX first; Quick decides promotion in active context and updates the marker before verification. Never guess from SVG content when §IX declares no data-driven object.

| Mode | `charts_index.json` keys | Notes |
|------|--------------------------|-------|
| `direct-calc` | `column_chart`, `horizontal_bar_chart`, `histogram_chart` | `calc bar`; `--horizontal` for horizontal bars; histogram bins are contiguous bars on the numeric x-axis |
| `direct-calc` | `line_chart`, `area_chart`, `scatter_chart` | `calc line`; area uses the line output as the top boundary, then closes to `y_max` |
| `direct-calc` | `pie_chart`, `donut_chart` | `calc pie`; donut passes `--inner-radius` |
| `direct-calc` | `radar_chart` | `calc radar` (separate subcommand) |
| `decomposable-calc` | `stacked_bar_chart`, `stacked_area_chart`, `grouped_bar_chart`, `dumbbell_chart`, `pareto_chart`, `dual_axis_line_chart`, `bullet_chart`, `butterfly_chart`, `waterfall_chart`, `box_plot_chart`, `gantt_chart`, `bar_of_pie_chart`, `pie_of_pie_chart`, `stock_chart` | Repeated direct calculations per the [verification recipes](../../scripts/docs/svg-pipeline.md#verification-recipes) |
| `partial-calc` | `bubble_chart`, `matrix_2x2` | `calc line` for x/y-driven `cx/cy`; radius only with an explicit size scale |
| `formula-verify` | `progress_bar_chart`, `gauge_chart`, `funnel_chart`, `sunburst_chart` | Quote the formula and resulting length/angle/width in the receipt |
| `manual-verify` | `sankey_chart`, `heatmap_chart`, `treemap_chart`, `word_cloud` | Data-driven, but no layout model; inspect and report |

**Family boundary**: this table covers every canonical `charts_index.json` key exactly once. Qualitative shape composition and Table references never enter the receipt merely because they contain shapes or numbers; named quadrants are composed through [`executor-structure.md`](../../references/executor-structure.md), and `chart/matrix_2x2` is reserved for plotted x/y data. Every embedded data chart is its own keyed §IX object.

If the list is empty, output `verify-charts: active profile declares no data-driven chart objects, nothing to verify` and stop.

## Step 2: Per object — read its SVG scope, calculate, compare, update

1. Read `<project_path>/svg_output/<page>.svg`; locate `<g id="<object-key>">` and its one plot-area marker (`chart-plot-area: object=<object-key> | …` inside `<g id="<object-key>-chartArea">`). A legacy unscoped marker with `id="chartArea"` is accepted only when the page has exactly one verified chart; a multi-chart page never mixes scoped and unscoped markers. Derive and add a missing scoped marker from the axes or center/radius before continuing.
2. Read only that object's data series and label/value elements.
3. **Read axis tick labels for every axis-based chart** — X-axis labels for horizontal bars, Y-axis labels for vertical bars and line-like charts. The first and last tick values give the axis range; pass it as attached `--value-range=min,max` / `--y-range=…` / `--x-range=…` (the attached form also protects a negative minimum). Radar takes `--max-value` from the outermost ring. With no tick labels, omit the range, let the calculator auto-normalize, and flag the receipt `scale=auto (no ticks)`; a deliberately hidden value axis takes its range from the native payload's axis minimum / maximum instead.
4. **Local vs absolute**: content inside `<g transform="translate(cx, cy)">` has relative coordinates; the calculator outputs absolute ones. Add the translate to the SVG values or subtract it from the calculator output — one direction, consistently.
5. Run the matching command (see the [calculator documentation](../../scripts/docs/svg-pipeline.md#svg_position_calculatorpy) and recipes for decomposable, partial, formula, and manual modes):

   ```bash
   python3 skills/ppt-master/scripts/svg_position_calculator.py calc bar --data "L1:V1,L2:V2" --area "x_min,y_min,x_max,y_max" --bar-width 120 --value-range=0,axis_max   # a Native-ready bar/column passes --gap-width <payload gap_width, default 150> instead of --bar-width so the category axis follows the PowerPoint slot model the parity gate checks
   python3 skills/ppt-master/scripts/svg_position_calculator.py calc line --data "x1:y1,x2:y2" --area "x_min,y_min,x_max,y_max" --y-range=0,max   # a Native-ready category line/area adds --slot-midpoints: PowerPoint centres each point in its category slot (payload `cross_between: "between"`); the edge-to-edge default is the scatter / numeric-axis model and a `mid_category` payload
   python3 skills/ppt-master/scripts/svg_position_calculator.py calc pie --data "S1:V1,S2:V2" --center "cx,cy" --radius 200 [--inner-radius 120] --start-angle -90
   python3 skills/ppt-master/scripts/svg_position_calculator.py calc radar --data "D1:V1,D2:V2,D3:V3" --center "cx,cy" --radius 200 --max-value 100
   ```

6. **Scale-aware comparison**: before declaring a mismatch, confirm every invocation used the axis range, plot area, center/radius, start angle, or size scale the SVG visually declares — for `calc bar` the header must show `Value scale: axis ticks (...)` when the SVG has ticks; `auto (max*1.1)` means go back to step 3. Never update the SVG with mismatched-scale output. When the scale matches and coordinates genuinely differ, update by hand — no regex or bulk replacement. On a signed bar chart the calculator starts every bar at the axis minimum, so compare `x_min + width` against the drawn far edge from the zero baseline rather than its `X`.

### Part 2: 一、改造任务完成情况

#### Slide 03 - 一、改造任务完成情况（一）：总体完成情况

- **Audience move**: 从"需要确认改造任务是否真的完成"到"认可四项总量指标同口径完成九成以上、总体判定为基本达标，并留下 5 个在建小区的追问点"
- **Relationships**: 计划量与完成量为 contrast（同一计量单位下的目标—实绩对照）；四项完成率互为 membership（同属总量完成率族，共用同一口径）；5 个在建小区与 63 个已竣工小区为 contrast
- **Composition**: 上部页标题与判断句；中部四条有界进度轨纵向排列（计划数、完成数、完成率、判定状态同行显示）；右侧窄栏为计划总盘子与口径说明
- **Title**: 改造任务总体完成情况
- **Core message**: 计划改造 68 个小区，已竣工验收 63 个，小区完工率 92.6%，四项总量指标按同一口径均为九成以上
- **Content**:
  - 判断句：三年改造任务总体完成九成以上，按统一判定阈值属"基本达标"，尚有 5 个小区在建。
  - 计划总盘子（2023—2025 年，2000 年底前建成老旧小区）：68 个小区、512 栋、2.14 万户、186.5 万平方米
  - 四项总量完成率（口径：完成数 ÷ 计划数 × 100%）：小区 63 个，完工率 92.6%，基本达标；楼栋 476 栋，完成率 93.0%，基本达标；居民户 1.98 万户，完成率 92.5%，基本达标；建筑面积 173.4 万平方米，完成率 93.0%，基本达标
  - 在建情况：在建 5 个小区、36 栋、1600 户、13.1 万平方米，占计划小区数 7.4%
  - 口径说明：完工率指已通过竣工验收的小区数占计划改造小区数的比例；"在建"指已开工未竣工；比率保留一位小数，全篇一致
- **Visualization**: 四项总量完成率进度轨（progress-tracks），子项为计划数、完成数、完成率数值与状态色标记；Native-ready: progress-tracks=no
- **Data class: scenario**（全部计划量、完成量与比率）

#### Slide 04 - 一、改造任务完成情况（二）：分项任务完成明细

- **Audience move**: 从"只知道总体完成率"到"看清九项分项任务中三项滞后、集中在完善类与提升类，为第四部分问题埋下依据"
- **Relationships**: 基础设施类、完善类、提升类为 parent，九项分项任务为 membership；各项完成率与统一判定阈值（95% / 90%）为 contrast；滞后三项（电梯、服务设施、停车泊位）互为并列，构成后续问题三的来源
- **Composition**: 整版表格：类别列合并显示三类，右侧六列为改造内容、单位、计划量、完成量、完成率、进度状态；表下为判定阈值口径行
- **Title**: 分项改造任务完成明细
- **Core message**: 九项分项任务中达标 1 项、基本达标 4 项、滞后 4 项，滞后项全部落在群众最关切的完善类与提升类
- **Content**:
  - 判断句：基础设施类总体完成，完善类与提升类三项任务完成率低于 90%，是总体完工率未能达标的主因。
  - 基础设施类：水电气路及雨污分流，个小区，计划 68，完成 63，92.6%，基本达标；光纤及 5G 覆盖，个小区，计划 68，完成 66，97.1%，达标
  - 完善类：加装电梯，部，计划 120，完成 96，80.0%，滞后；新增停车泊位，个，计划 3200，完成 2860，89.4%，滞后；电动自行车充电设施，处，计划 260，完成 241，92.7%，基本达标；无障碍及适老化改造，处，计划 180，完成 163，90.6%，基本达标
  - 提升类：社区服务及养老托幼设施，处，计划 24，完成 19，79.2%，滞后；智慧安防（视频监控、门禁），个小区，计划 68，完成 61，89.7%，滞后；绿化及公共空间，万平方米，计划 15.6，完成 14.1，90.4%，基本达标
  - 判定口径：≥95% 达标、90%（含）—95% 基本达标、<90% 滞后，与 P02 纲要及 P08 满意度维度使用同一阈值
  - 汇总行：九项分项任务，达标 1 项、基本达标 4 项、滞后 4 项
- **Visualization**: 分项任务完成明细表（subtask-metric-table），子项为类别分组行、九项任务行、汇总行与状态色标；Native-ready: subtask-metric-table=yes
- **Data class: scenario**（全部计划量、完成量、完成率与判定结果）

### Part 3: 二、资金使用情况

### Part 2: 一、改造任务完成情况

#### Slide 03 - 一、改造任务完成情况（一）：总体完成情况

- **Audience move**: 从"需要确认改造任务是否真的完成"到"认可四项总量指标同口径完成九成以上、总体判定为基本达标，并留下 5 个在建小区的追问点"
- **Relationships**: 计划量与完成量为 contrast（同一计量单位下的目标—实绩对照）；四项完成率互为 membership（同属总量完成率族，共用同一口径）；5 个在建小区与 63 个已竣工小区为 contrast
- **Composition**: 上部页标题与判断句；中部四条有界进度轨纵向排列（计划数、完成数、完成率、判定状态同行显示）；右侧窄栏为计划总盘子与口径说明
- **Title**: 改造任务总体完成情况
- **Core message**: 计划改造 68 个小区，已竣工验收 63 个，小区完工率 92.6%，四项总量指标按同一口径均为九成以上
- **Content**:
  - 判断句：三年改造任务总体完成九成以上，按统一判定阈值属"基本达标"，尚有 5 个小区在建。
  - 计划总盘子（2023—2025 年，2000 年底前建成老旧小区）：68 个小区、512 栋、2.14 万户、186.5 万平方米
  - 四项总量完成率（口径：完成数 ÷ 计划数 × 100%）：小区 63 个，完工率 92.6%，基本达标；楼栋 476 栋，完成率 93.0%，基本达标；居民户 1.98 万户，完成率 92.5%，基本达标；建筑面积 173.4 万平方米，完成率 93.0%，基本达标
  - 在建情况：在建 5 个小区、36 栋、1600 户、13.1 万平方米，占计划小区数 7.4%
  - 口径说明：完工率指已通过竣工验收的小区数占计划改造小区数的比例；"在建"指已开工未竣工；比率保留一位小数，全篇一致
- **Visualization**: 四项总量完成率进度轨（progress-tracks），子项为计划数、完成数、完成率数值与状态色标记；Native-ready: progress-tracks=no
- **Data class: scenario**（全部计划量、完成量与比率）

#### Slide 04 - 一、改造任务完成情况（二）：分项任务完成明细

- **Audience move**: 从"只知道总体完成率"到"看清九项分项任务中三项滞后、集中在完善类与提升类，为第四部分问题埋下依据"
- **Relationships**: 基础设施类、完善类、提升类为 parent，九项分项任务为 membership；各项完成率与统一判定阈值（95% / 90%）为 contrast；滞后三项（电梯、服务设施、停车泊位）互为并列，构成后续问题三的来源
- **Composition**: 整版表格：类别列合并显示三类，右侧六列为改造内容、单位、计划量、完成量、完成率、进度状态；表下为判定阈值口径行
- **Title**: 分项改造任务完成明细
- **Core message**: 九项分项任务中达标 1 项、基本达标 4 项、滞后 4 项，滞后项全部落在群众最关切的完善类与提升类
- **Content**:
  - 判断句：基础设施类总体完成，完善类与提升类三项任务完成率低于 90%，是总体完工率未能达标的主因。
  - 基础设施类：水电气路及雨污分流，个小区，计划 68，完成 63，92.6%，基本达标；光纤及 5G 覆盖，个小区，计划 68，完成 66，97.1%，达标
  - 完善类：加装电梯，部，计划 120，完成 96，80.0%，滞后；新增停车泊位，个，计划 3200，完成 2860，89.4%，滞后；电动自行车充电设施，处，计划 260，完成 241，92.7%，基本达标；无障碍及适老化改造，处，计划 180，完成 163，90.6%，基本达标
  - 提升类：社区服务及养老托幼设施，处，计划 24，完成 19，79.2%，滞后；智慧安防（视频监控、门禁），个小区，计划 68，完成 61，89.7%，滞后；绿化及公共空间，万平方米，计划 15.6，完成 14.1，90.4%，基本达标
  - 判定口径：≥95% 达标、90%（含）—95% 基本达标、<90% 滞后，与 P02 纲要及 P08 满意度维度使用同一阈值
  - 汇总行：九项分项任务，达标 1 项、基本达标 4 项、滞后 4 项
- **Visualization**: 分项任务完成明细表（subtask-metric-table），子项为类别分组行、九项任务行、汇总行与状态色标；Native-ready: subtask-metric-table=yes
- **Data class: scenario**（全部计划量、完成量、完成率与判定结果）

### Part 3: 二、资金使用情况

#### Slide 05 - 二、资金使用情况（一）：资金到位与支出执行总体情况

- **Audience move**: 从"关心钱有没有到位、有没有花出去"到"掌握 42800 万元计划投资的到位、支出、结余三段流转与三项比率，注意到 5393 万元结余尚未形成实物工作量"
- **Relationships**: 计划总投资、到位缺口、实际到位、已支出、账面积余为 order（资金流转顺序，正负贡献串联）；到位率、支出执行率、结余率为同族 membership（分母各不相同，须并列说明）；已支出与账面积余为 contrast
- **Composition**: 上部页标题与判断句；中部左侧为瀑布式资金流转几何（五段，正负以语义色区分），右侧竖排四个 KPI（计划总投资、到位率、支出执行率、结余率）；下部为三项比率的分母口径对照行
- **Title**: 资金到位与支出执行总体情况
- **Core message**: 计划总投资 42800 万元，实际到位 38520 万元、到位率 90.0%；已支出 33127 万元、支出执行率 86.0%；账面积余 5393 万元、结余率 14.0%
- **Content**:
  - 判断句：资金到位九成、支出执行八成六，尚有 5393 万元结余资金未形成实物工作量。
  - 计划总投资 42800 万元（4.28 亿元）；实际到位 38520 万元，到位缺口 4280 万元，资金到位率 90.0%
  - 已支出（已拨付）33127 万元，支出执行率 86.0%；账面积余 5393 万元，结余率 14.0%
  - 户均投入：按已到位资金与已完成户数计算，户均 1.9 万元（38520 万元 ÷ 1.98 万户）
  - 比率口径对照（全篇一致）：资金到位率 = 实际到位 ÷ 计划总投资 × 100% = 90.0%；支出执行率 = 已支出 ÷ 实际到位 × 100% = 86.0%；结余率 = 账面积余 ÷ 实际到位 × 100% = 14.0%
  - 金额单位统一为万元，比率保留一位小数
- **Visualization**: 资金流转瀑布（fund-flow-waterfall），子项为五段金额标注、正负贡献方向与差额连线；Native-ready: fund-flow-waterfall=yes
- **Data class: scenario**（全部金额、比率与户均投入）

#### Slide 06 - 二、资金使用情况（二）：资金来源与支出构成明细

- **Audience move**: 从"知道总体到位率 90.0%"到"看清 4280 万元缺口全部来自区级配套、社会资本与居民出资三个渠道，以及提升类支出执行率 75.9% 最低"
- **Relationships**: 资金来源（六渠道）与资金支出（四分项）为并列 parent，各自渠道/分项为 membership，均含小计与合计；三级财政补助（100.0%）与区级配套（81.8%）、社会资本（73.0%）、居民出资（65.8%）为 contrast；提升类支出执行率（75.9%）与提升类任务完成率（79.2%、89.7%、90.4%）为跨页 link
- **Composition**: 整版分层表格：上半组"资金来源"六行加小计，下半组"资金支出"四行加小计，右侧窄栏为资金监管三条与审计、公示比率
- **Title**: 资金来源与支出构成明细
- **Core message**: 三级财政补助资金 100.0% 到位，区级配套 81.8%、社会资本 73.0%、居民出资 65.8%，构成 4280 万元缺口的全部来源；支出侧提升类执行率 75.9% 为四类最低
- **Content**:
  - 判断句：资金缺口全部产生于区级配套与社会、居民出资三个渠道，支出侧提升类执行最慢。
  - 资金来源（计划数 / 到位数 / 到位率 / 缺口数，单位万元）：中央补助资金 7704 / 7704 / 100.0% / 0；省级补助资金 4622 / 4622 / 100.0% / 0；市级财政资金 11556 / 11556 / 100.0% / 0；区级财政配套 11770 / 9630 / 81.8% / 2140；管线单位及社会资本 4222 / 3082 / 73.0% / 1140；居民出资 2926 / 1926 / 65.8% / 1000；来源合计 42800 / 38520 / 90.0% / 4280
  - 资金支出（资金安排数 / 已支出数 / 支出执行率 / 结余数，单位万元）：基础设施类 18490 / 16564 / 89.6% / 1926；完善类（含加装电梯）11556 / 9938 / 86.0% / 1618；提升类 6548 / 4969 / 75.9% / 1579；前期及管理费 1926 / 1656 / 86.0% / 270；支出合计 38520 / 33127 / 86.0% / 5393
  - 表内口径：来源组"执行"为实际到位、比率为到位率（分母为计划数）；支出组"执行"为已支出、比率为支出执行率（分母为该类资金安排数，安排数合计等于已到位资金 38520 万元）
  - 资金监管三条：专户核算、专款专用（68 个小区全部纳入专户，覆盖率 100%）；全过程跟踪审计（已完成审计 41 个项目，占已竣工项目 65.1%）；资金使用情况按小区公示（68 个，公示率 100%）
  - 结余构成：5393 万元中 3236 万元因竣工结算审计未完成暂不能拨付，占结余总额 60.0%
- **Visualization**: 资金来源与支出分层明细表（fund-hierarchy-table），子项为两组分层行、小计与合计行、到位率/执行率状态色标；Native-ready: fund-hierarchy-table=yes
- **Data class: scenario**（全部金额、比率、审计与公示数据）

=== §IX 判断句 ===
45:- **Mode Behavior**: 公文化汇报体。每页以一句判断句（结论前置，源自 pyramid）统领本页事实，随后按公文条目化方式完整、均衡、可扫读地铺陈数据、表格与口径说明（源自 briefing），不作渲染性论述、不设悬念；页面标题一律使用"（一）（二）"式公文章节题名；末章集中提出审议请求与目标口径，形成"结论—依据—问题—措施—审议"的闭环。
48:- **Visual Style Behavior**: 严格左对齐栅格与 1px 细分隔线，无阴影、无发光、无圆角堆叠（圆角 2px）、无装饰性图形与插画。页眉为"章节编号 + 章名 + 页码"的公文式页眉带（赭金编号、深藏青章名、下缘 1px 分隔线），页脚为"数据来源 + 统计口径 + 数据截至日"的来源行（源自 data-journalism 的 source line 传统）。数据一律以原生表格与条形/瀑布几何呈现，白底为主、浅灰面板为辅，语义色仅用于状态判定（达标/基本达标/滞后），版面留白充裕但信息密度按页承载完整判断句与依据。
103:- **Hierarchy direction**: 页眉章节带（定位）→ 页标题与判断句（本页结论）→ 主数据区（表格/图表/KPI）→ 口径与状态注解 → 页脚来源行；视线自上而下、自左而右，结论先于依据。
104:- **Composition tendency**: 内容页以"左结论右依据"或"上判断句下数据面"为主；数据页优先整版表格或整版条形几何，配一条窄侧栏放口径说明；问题页采用"问题—数据溯源—影响"三段式对应结构，使来源指向可读。
221:- **Composition**: 上部页标题与判断句；中部四条有界进度轨纵向排列（计划数、完成数、完成率、判定状态同行显示）；右侧窄栏为计划总盘子与口径说明
225:  - 判断句：三年改造任务总体完成九成以上，按统一判定阈值属"基本达标"，尚有 5 个小区在建。
241:  - 判断句：基础设施类总体完成，完善类与提升类三项任务完成率低于 90%，是总体完工率未能达标的主因。
256:- **Composition**: 上部页标题与判断句；中部左侧为瀑布式资金流转几何（五段，正负以语义色区分），右侧竖排四个 KPI（计划总投资、到位率、支出执行率、结余率）；下部为三项比率的分母口径对照行
260:  - 判断句：资金到位九成、支出执行八成六，尚有 5393 万元结余资金未形成实物工作量。
277:  - 判断句：资金缺口全部产生于区级配套与社会、居民出资三个渠道，支出侧提升类执行最慢。
296:  - 判断句：总体满意度 93.8%，其中满意 71.2%、基本满意 22.6%、不满意 6.2%。
313:  - 判断句：满意度总体较高但结构不平衡，三个短板维度全部指向完善类任务与施工期管理。
329:  - 判断句：诉求办结率 85.7%，未办结事项高度集中，前两类占 64.1%。
348:  - 判断句：资金方面的两个问题，一个出在来源结构、一个出在支出进度，直接影响了完工率与提升类任务。
366:  - 判断句：实施与群众工作方面的三个问题，全部能在第一部分完成率与第三部分满意度数据中找到对应项。
388:  - 判断句：五个问题对应七项措施，目标值、时限、责任单位逐条落地。
409:  - 判断句：整改之外同步建立长效机制，并提请评审组审议三项事项。
424:- **Content**: 每页讲稿包含四段——本页判断句复述、数据口径说明（分母与保留位数）、与前后页的呼应关系（尤其问题页须点明数据出处页）、面向专家质询的预备答复要点；所有数值只引用页面已出现的同一口径数据，不引入新数字；公文语体，不使用口语化表达
426:- **Notes style**: formal（公文汇报语体，判断句 + 依据 + 口径 + 请审议）

15:| Core Message / Ask / Action | 三年改造任务总体完成九成以上，资金到位率 90.0%、支出执行率 86.0%，居民满意度 93.8%；尚未闭合的 4280 万元资金缺口与三个低于 90% 的满意度短板维度，就是全部五个问题的来源；下一步以七项措施把五项比率推到 100%、100%、98% 以上、100%、95% 以上，提请评审组审议三项事项 |
164:| P07 | chart | donut_chart | 满意、基本满意、不满意三档评价构成总体满意度 100% |
195:  - 口径脚注：本汇报数据截至 2026 年 8 月 31 日；比率均以"完成（到位、支出、满意）数 ÷ 计划（到位）数 × 100%"计算，保留一位小数
206:  - 一、改造任务完成情况（P03—P04）｜口径：完成率 = 完成数 ÷ 计划数 × 100%｜小区完工率 92.6%
207:  - 二、资金使用情况（P05—P06）｜口径：到位率 = 到位数 ÷ 计划总投资 × 100%；支出执行率 = 已支出数 ÷ 已到位数 × 100%｜到位率 90.0%、支出执行率 86.0%
208:  - 三、居民满意度（P07—P09）｜口径：满意度 =（满意 + 基本满意）÷ 有效问卷 × 100%｜总体满意度 93.8%、诉求办结率 85.7%
219:- **Audience move**: 从"需要确认改造任务是否真的完成"到"认可四项总量指标同口径完成九成以上、总体判定为基本达标，并留下 5 个在建小区的追问点"
223:- **Core message**: 计划改造 68 个小区，已竣工验收 63 个，小区完工率 92.6%，四项总量指标按同一口径均为九成以上
225:  - 判断句：三年改造任务总体完成九成以上，按统一判定阈值属"基本达标"，尚有 5 个小区在建。
227:  - 四项总量完成率（口径：完成数 ÷ 计划数 × 100%）：小区 63 个，完工率 92.6%，基本达标；楼栋 476 栋，完成率 93.0%，基本达标；居民户 1.98 万户，完成率 92.5%，基本达标；建筑面积 173.4 万平方米，完成率 93.0%，基本达标
235:- **Audience move**: 从"只知道总体完成率"到"看清九项分项任务中三项滞后、集中在完善类与提升类，为第四部分问题埋下依据"
236:- **Relationships**: 基础设施类、完善类、提升类为 parent，九项分项任务为 membership；各项完成率与统一判定阈值（95% / 90%）为 contrast；滞后三项（电梯、服务设施、停车泊位）互为并列，构成后续问题三的来源
260:  - 判断句：资金到位九成、支出执行八成六，尚有 5393 万元结余资金未形成实物工作量。
264:  - 比率口径对照（全篇一致）：资金到位率 = 实际到位 ÷ 计划总投资 × 100% = 90.0%；支出执行率 = 已支出 ÷ 实际到位 × 100% = 86.0%；结余率 = 账面积余 ÷ 实际到位 × 100% = 14.0%
281:  - 资金监管三条：专户核算、专款专用（68 个小区全部纳入专户，覆盖率 100%）；全过程跟踪审计（已完成审计 41 个项目，占已竣工项目 65.1%）；资金使用情况按小区公示（68 个，公示率 100%）
291:- **Relationships**: 满意、基本满意、不满意三档为 membership（合计 100%）；满意及以上（93.8%）与不满意（6.2%）为 contrast；调查组织要素（机构、时间、方式、样本）与总体结果为 parent→membership
299:  - 满意度口径：满意度 =（满意 + 基本满意）÷ 有效问卷 × 100%，分维度满意度使用同一口径；不满意 6.2% 对应 385 份问卷
300:  - 群众参与：改造方案公示 68 个小区，公示率 100%；召开居民议事会 214 场
331:  - 办理总量：收集 1286 条，已办结 1102 条，办结率 85.7%（口径：已办结 ÷ 收集总数 × 100%），未办结 184 条
389:  - 措施 1（对应问题一）：报请区政府追加 2026 年度区级配套预算，签订管线单位共建共担协议 3 家，居民出资实行"一小区一方案"分摊｜资金到位率 90.0% → 100%（补齐缺口 4280 万元：区级 2140、社会资本 1140、居民 1000）｜2026 年 10 月底前区级到位、12 月底前社会及居民出资到位｜区财政局、区住建局、各街道

### Part 4: 三、居民满意度

#### Slide 07 - 三、居民满意度（一）：调查组织与总体结果

- **Audience move**: 从"怀疑满意度是否可信"到"确认第三方调查的样本、方式、口径可核，总体满意度 93.8% 成立"
- **Relationships**: 满意、基本满意、不满意三档为 membership（合计 100%）；满意及以上（93.8%）与不满意（6.2%）为 contrast；调查组织要素（机构、时间、方式、样本）与总体结果为 parent→membership
- **Composition**: breathing 页——左侧大号满意度数字与环形构成，右侧为调查组织与口径四条短陈述，版面留白加倍
- **Title**: 居民满意度调查总体结果
- **Core message**: 第三方调查覆盖 68 个小区、有效问卷 6214 份，总体满意度 93.8%
- **Content**:
  - 判断句：总体满意度 93.8%，其中满意 71.2%、基本满意 22.6%、不满意 6.2%。
  - 调查组织：委托第三方机构（区社情民意调查中心）于 2026 年 6—7 月开展，覆盖全部 68 个改造小区
  - 调查方式与样本：入户问卷与线上问卷并行，发放 6800 份，回收有效问卷 6214 份，有效回收率 91.4%
  - 满意度口径：满意度 =（满意 + 基本满意）÷ 有效问卷 × 100%，分维度满意度使用同一口径；不满意 6.2% 对应 385 份问卷
  - 群众参与：改造方案公示 68 个小区，公示率 100%；召开居民议事会 214 场
  - 评价说明：本页与 P08 分维度结果均来自同一次调查、同一份有效问卷库，不可跨调查混用
- **Visualization**: 满意度构成环形图（satisfaction-donut），子项为三档占比、中心总体满意度数字与图例；Native-ready: satisfaction-donut=yes
- **Data class: scenario**（问卷数、比率、场次与机构名称）

### Part 5: 四、存在问题

#### Slide 10 - 四、存在问题（一）：资金保障与支出进度方面

- **Audience move**: 从"等待被指出问题"到"看到两个资金类问题均由汇报方主动列出，并逐条标注第二部分的具体比率与金额出处"
- **Relationships**: 问题一、问题二为并列（同属资金方面）；每个问题下"问题表现—数据溯源—造成影响"为 parent→membership 且三段为 order；数据溯源与 P05、P06 的资金比率为 link；造成影响与 P03、P04 的完成率为 link
- **Composition**: 上下两块问题带，每块内部左为问题编号与题名、中为问题表现与数据溯源（引用具体比率并标注出处页）、右为造成影响；块底一条细线指向"来源：第二部分 资金使用情况"
- **Title**: 存在问题（一）：资金保障与支出进度方面
- **Core message**: 两个资金类问题分别来自"到位率 90.0% 的渠道结构"与"支出执行率 86.0% 的进度差"，均可回溯至 P05、P06 数据
- **Content**:
  - 判断句：资金方面的两个问题，一个出在来源结构、一个出在支出进度，直接影响了完工率与提升类任务。
  - 问题一：多元筹资渠道尚未闭合，区级配套与社会、居民出资到位率偏低
  - 问题一数据溯源（P06）：区级财政配套到位率 81.8%（缺口 2140 万元）、管线单位及社会资本到位率 73.0%（缺口 1140 万元）、居民出资到位率 65.8%（缺口 1000 万元），而中央、省级、市级三级补助资金到位率均为 100.0%
  - 问题一造成影响（P03、P04）：整体资金到位率 90.0%；5 个在建小区中 4 个因资金未闭合缓建，直接使小区完工率停在 92.6%
  - 问题二：支出进度滞后于到位进度，结余资金沉淀未形成实物工作量
  - 问题二数据溯源（P05、P06）：支出执行率 86.0%，账面积余 5393 万元、结余率 14.0%；分类支出执行率提升类 75.9%、完善类与前期及管理费 86.0%、基础设施类 89.6%；5393 万元中 3236 万元因竣工结算审计未完成暂不能拨付，占结余 60.0%
  - 问题二造成影响（P04）：提升类支出执行率最低，对应提升类任务完成率最低——社区服务及养老托幼设施 79.2%、智慧安防 89.7%
  - 问题成因（资金侧）：竣工结算审计周期平均 92 天，已审计项目 41 个、占已竣工项目 65.1%，审计滞后是结余沉淀的直接原因
- **Data class: scenario**（问题表述所引全部比率、金额与比例关系）

#### Slide 11 - 四、存在问题（二）：改造实施与群众诉求方面

- **Audience move**: 从"认可资金问题"到"确认实施与群众工作方面三个问题同样有出处，且逐条对应第一部分完成率与第三部分满意度维度、诉求分类"
- **Relationships**: 问题三、问题四、问题五为并列（同属实施与群众诉求方面）；每个问题下"问题表现—数据溯源—满意度呼应"为 parent→membership；问题三与 P04 完成率、P08 短板维度为 link；问题四与 P08 最低维度、P09 施工期诉求为 link；问题五与 P09 物业衔接诉求为 link
- **Composition**: 三栏问题卡横向并列，每卡自上而下为问题编号与题名、问题表现、数据溯源（标注出处页）、满意度或任务呼应；卡底一条统一的"来源指向"细线，分别指向第一部分与第三部分
- **Title**: 存在问题（二）：改造实施与群众诉求方面
- **Core message**: 三个问题分别对应完善类与提升类任务滞后、施工期现场管理不足、改造与管护衔接缺位，出处依次为 P04、P08、P09
- **Content**:
  - 判断句：实施与群众工作方面的三个问题，全部能在第一部分完成率与第三部分满意度数据中找到对应项。
  - 问题三：完善类、提升类任务推进不平衡，滞后项集中在群众最关切事项
  - 问题三数据溯源（P04）：加装电梯完成率 80.0%、社区服务及养老托幼设施 79.2%、新增停车泊位 89.4%、智慧安防 89.7%，均低于总体完工率 92.6%
  - 问题三满意度呼应（P08）：加装电梯推进 84.6%、停车与充电设施 82.1%，为七个维度中最低两项；未办结诉求中电梯与停车两类合计 118 条、占 64.1%（P09）
  - 问题四：施工期现场管理不到位，直接影响群众感受
  - 问题四数据溯源（P08、P09）：施工期文明管理（噪声、扬尘、通行）满意度 79.4%，为全维度最低；未办结诉求中施工期噪声扬尘 32 条、占 17.4%
  - 问题四问题表现：部分项目未落实公示告知、错峰施工与扬尘抑制措施；68 个小区配备现场监督员 42 名，覆盖率 61.8%
  - 问题五：改造与后续管护衔接不够，长效机制尚未建立
  - 问题五数据溯源（P09）：未办结诉求中"配套设施及物业衔接"34 条、占 18.5%
  - 问题五问题表现：63 个已完工小区中 45 个落实物业服务、覆盖率 71.4%，其余 18 个仍由社区代管；后续管护资金渠道未明确
- **Data class: scenario**（问题表述所引全部比率、条数与覆盖率）

  - 问题一造成影响（P03、P04）：整体资金到位率 90.0%；5 个在建小区中 4 个因资金未闭合缓建，直接使小区完工率停在 92.6%
  - 问题二：支出进度滞后于到位进度，结余资金沉淀未形成实物工作量
  - 问题二数据溯源（P05、P06）：支出执行率 86.0%，账面积余 5393 万元、结余率 14.0%；分类支出执行率提升类 75.9%、完善类与前期及管理费 86.0%、基础设施类 89.6%；5393 万元中 3236 万元因竣工结算审计未完成暂不能拨付，占结余 60.0%

  - 问题成因（资金侧）：竣工结算审计周期平均 92 天，已审计项目 41 个、占已竣工项目 65.1%，审计滞后是结余沉淀的直接原因

- **Core message**: 两个资金类问题分别来自"到位率 90.0% 的渠道结构"与"支出执行率 86.0% 的进度差"，均可回溯至 P05、P06 数据

  - 问题一数据溯源（P06）：区级财政配套到位率 81.8%（缺口 2140 万元）、管线单位及社会资本到位率 73.0%（缺口 1140 万元）、居民出资到位率 65.8%（缺口 1000 万元），而中央、省级、市级三级补助资金到位率均为 100.0%
  - 问题一造成影响（P03、P04）：整体资金到位率 90.0%；5 个在建小区中 4 个因资金未闭合缓建，直接使小区完工率停在 92.6%
  - 问题二：支出进度滞后于到位进度，结余资金沉淀未形成实物工作量
  - 问题二数据溯源（P05、P06）：支出执行率 86.0%，账面积余 5393 万元、结余率 14.0%；分类支出执行率提升类 75.9%、完善类与前期及管理费 86.0%、基础设施类 89.6%；5393 万元中 3236 万元因竣工结算审计未完成暂不能拨付，占结余 60.0%
  - 问题二造成影响（P04）：提升类支出执行率最低，对应提升类任务完成率最低——社区服务及养老托幼设施 79.2%、智慧安防 89.7%
  - 问题成因（资金侧）：竣工结算审计周期平均 92 天，已审计项目 41 个、占已竣工项目 65.1%，审计滞后是结余沉淀的直接原因

  - 措施 1（对应问题一）：报请区政府追加 2026 年度区级配套预算，签订管线单位共建共担协议 3 家，居民出资实行"一小区一方案"分摊｜资金到位率 90.0% → 100%（补齐缺口 4280 万元：区级 2140、社会资本 1140、居民 1000）｜2026 年 10 月底前区级到位、12 月底前社会及居民出资到位｜区财政局、区住建局、各街道
  - 措施 2（对应问题二）：建立"竣工一个、结算一个、审计一个"机制，压缩结算审计周期｜平均审计周期 92 天 → 45 天；支出执行率 86.0% → 98.0% 以上，消化结余 5393 万元｜2026 年 12 月底前｜区审计局、区财政局、区住建局
  - 措施 3（对应问题三）：5 个在建小区实行"一小区一策"清单化推进｜小区完工率 92.6% → 100%（剩余 5 个、36 栋、1600 户、13.1 万平方米）｜2026 年 11 月底前｜各街道、区住建局、代建单位
  - 措施 4（对应问题三）：加装电梯攻坚与停车资源挖潜｜电梯 96 部 → 120 部（完成率 80.0% → 100%）；停车泊位 2860 个 → 3200 个（89.4% → 100%）；充电设施 241 处 → 260 处（92.7% → 100%）｜2027 年 6 月底前｜区住建局、区规划资源分局、各街道
  - 措施 5（对应问题三）：补齐提升类设施短板｜社区服务及养老托幼设施 19 处 → 24 处（79.2% → 100%）；智慧安防 61 个 → 68 个（89.7% → 100%）；绿化及公共空间 14.1 万㎡ → 15.6 万㎡（90.4% → 100%）｜2027 年 6 月底前｜区民政局、区住建局、各街道
  - 措施 6（对应问题四）：施工期文明管理"三个一"（一张告示、一名监督员、一个投诉电话），未办结诉求台账销号｜现场监督员覆盖率 61.8% → 100%；诉求办结率 85.7% → 100%；施工期文明管理满意度 79.4% → 90% 以上｜2026 年 12 月底前｜各街道、区住建局、施工单位
  - 措施 7（对应问题五）："改造 + 物业"衔接，明确管护资金渠道并建立年度回访｜已完工小区物业服务覆盖率 71.4% → 100%（45 个 → 63 个）；总体满意度保持 95% 以上｜2026 年 12 月底前｜区住建局、区房管部门、各街道
  - 表下口径行：目标值一律以"现状 → 目标"表述，现状值取自 P03—P09 同一口径数据，不另设统计范围

- **Relationships**: 三项长效机制为并列 membership（管护、评价、监督）；三项提请审议事项为 order（须逐项表决）；总体目标五项比率与 P03—P09 现状值为 link（现状 → 目标）
- **Composition**: 上部为三项长效机制横向并列，中部为总体目标口径带（五项比率现状 → 目标），下部为三项提请审议事项编号列出，收尾一行结束语句

- **Title**: 长效管护机制与提请审议事项
- **Core message**: 建立"改造—管护—评价"闭环，提请评审组审议三项事项
- **Content**:
  - 判断句：整改之外同步建立长效机制，并提请评审组审议三项事项。
  - 长效机制一（管护）：完工小区竣工即移交物业服务，管护资金由物业服务费、小区公共收益与财政补贴三渠道明确分担
  - 长效机制二（评价）：每季度开展满意度回访，年度公布改造绩效，回访口径与本次调查一致（满意度 =（满意 + 基本满意）÷ 有效问卷 × 100%）
  - 长效机制三（监督）：资金全过程跟踪审计与按小区公示常态化，公示率保持 100%，审计覆盖率由 65.1% 提升至 100%
  - 总体目标（至 2027 年 6 月底，同口径）：小区完工率 92.6% → 100%；资金到位率 90.0% → 100%；支出执行率 86.0% → 98% 以上；诉求办结率 85.7% → 100%；居民总体满意度 93.8% → 95% 以上
  - 提请审议事项一：同意追加区级配套资金 2140 万元并纳入 2026 年度财政预算
  - 提请审议事项二：同意 5 个在建小区竣工时限调整至 2026 年 11 月底
  - 提请审议事项三：支持将管线单位"共建共担"机制纳入市级文件，明确社会与居民出资分担规则
  - 结束语：以上汇报，提请评审组审议。

### Part 2: 一、改造任务完成情况

#### Slide 03 - 一、改造任务完成情况（一）：总体完成情况

- **Title**: 改造任务总体完成情况
- **Core message**: 计划改造 68 个小区，累计开工 68 个、开工率 100.0%，已竣工验收 63 个、小区完工率 92.6%，四项总量完成率按同一口径均落在 92.5%—93.0% 区间

- **Composition**: 上部页标题与判断句；中部四条有界进度轨纵向排列（指标名、计划与完成量、完成率数值与判定状态同行显示，轨上标注 90%／95%／100% 判定刻度与基本达标区间）；右侧窄栏为计划总盘子、在建情况与总体判定
- **Title**: 改造任务总体完成情况
- **Core message**: 计划改造 68 个小区，累计开工 68 个、开工率 100.0%，已竣工验收 63 个、小区完工率 92.6%，四项总量完成率按同一口径均落在 92.5%—93.0% 区间

  - 判断句：累计开工68个小区、开工率100.0%；完工63个、完工率92.6%，按统一判定阈值属"基本达标"。
  - 完成率标尺：0—100%，标注 90%（滞后线）、95%（达标线）、100% 三个判定刻度，90%—95% 为基本达标区间
  - 计划总盘子（2023—2025 年，2000 年底前建成老旧小区）：改造小区 68 个、涉及楼栋 512 栋、涉及居民 2.14 万户、建筑面积 186.5 万平方米
  - 四项总量完成率（口径：完成数 ÷ 计划数 × 100%）：改造小区（个）计划 68／已竣工 63，92.6%，基本达标；改造楼栋（栋）计划 512／已完成 476，93.0%，基本达标；惠及居民（万户）计划 2.14／已完成 1.98，92.5%，基本达标；建筑面积（万平方米）计划 186.5／已完成 173.4，93.0%，基本达标
  - 在建情况：在建 5 个小区、36 栋、1600 户、13.1 万平方米，占计划 7.4%
  - 总体判定：四项总量完成率均落在 90%—95% 区间，按统一阈值判定为基本达标
  - 口径说明：完工率＝已通过竣工验收小区数÷计划改造小区数；"在建"指已开工未竣工；比率保留一位小数，全篇一致

# Executor Speaker-notes Branch

Conditional late-stage authority for generating or validating the complete speaker-notes document.

**Trigger**: Default loads this after the final quality check when the effective Speaker Notes outcome in `design_spec.md §I` is enabled (a missing legacy outcome defaults to enabled); Quick loads it after its final check when the agent selected notes or narration. Narration requires notes; with notes disabled, do not load this branch or create `notes/total.md`.

## 1. Complete Speaker-notes Document

Write the whole deck to `notes/total.md` in one batch: `# <number>_<page_title>` per page (`# Slide <number>` only for a script written before the roster exists; the splitter takes both), `---` between pages; only the heading is stripped before TTS. `notes_to_audio.py` reads the body verbatim, so write prose only — no list/bullet markup, stage markers, key-point labels, duration lines, or other metadata. Keep one language unless the confirmed contract is bilingual — then every page keeps the same segment order (first language, blank line, second language; narration reads both and doubles the page's time, so notes headed for audio keep one language unless both are meant to be heard); spell out digits or symbols when literal TTS would sound wrong (Chinese "百分之六十八" rather than "68%").

**Pre-SVG narration branch**: when `notes/total.md` already exists from a final/literal script or Quick direct narrated video, validate it instead of regenerating. Retain every word and segment of a final/literal script; agent-authored Quick narration may be repaired only for final-SVG inconsistency and before audio. A `# Slide <number>` heading remains valid until Generate Step 7.1 resolves the roster.

**Length follows content**: size natural sentences to semantic burden — two to five is typical, not a cap; anchor pages may use less and dense pages more. Duration is pacing guidance only: never pad, repeat, compress, or omit meaning to hit it.

## 2. Final-SVG Grounding and Coverage

**Hard rule — the final SVG is the visible page authority**: read every finalized `svg_output/<slide>.svg` in slide order with the active plan/context and approved sources; never write from the outline or core message alone.

Before drafting, internally inventory the visible title/subtitle and every information-bearing direct-root `<g id>` (structured placeholder content counts). Coverage means its unique claim, evidence, example, relationship, qualifier, or implication — not merely its label — enters the narration. For a pre-SVG script, apply the inventory in reverse: every independent visible claim is supported by its script segment; repair the visual page or return to planning for final/literal input, repair the narration before audio for agent-authored Quick narration, and give every spoken idea needing orientation a visible state or explicit speech-only role.

- Text blocks, comparisons, and processes keep every independent fact or relationship; combine related short groups causally or comparatively.
- Charts, tables, and KPIs state the takeaway, decisive values or trend, comparison basis, implication, and material uncertainty — not every axis, row, or cell.
- Quotes keep the decisive clause, material attribution, and relevance. Explain semantic images or text-free diagrams only from the SVG plus plan/source; never infer facts from appearance.
- Speak a source or footer only when attribution, uncertainty, or qualification changes the argument. Omit backgrounds, decoration, chrome, page numbers, and fixed Master/Layout atoms.

Form one coherent argument in intended reading/reveal order — proposition → evidence or mechanism → implication or bridge; DOM order need not be speaking order. A sentence may cover related groups and a complex group may need several sentences, but no independent group disappears to meet a count. Never vocalize IDs, positions, colors, icons, "this card shows" descriptions, or coverage markers.

## 3. Reading Mode and TTS

| `consumption_mode` | Notes emphasis |
|---|---|
| `text` | Interpret and connect a self-contained page; synthesize every independent information group rather than omitting it |
| `balanced` | Connect visible claim and evidence, explain the trade-off, bridge forward |
| `presentation` | Carry reasoning, context, and supporting detail intentionally omitted from the sparse page |

Put transitions naturally in the opening sentence when useful; never label them. When `notes/total.md` is complete, return to Generate Step 7.1 (Default) or `quick-generate.md` §4 (Quick); each route owns splitting and its success criterion.
